Measure documents against an instrument

measure.Rd

Runs every item in the instrument against every document and returns the probabilities in $probs, one row per document, item and label, beside $calls, one row per document and item.

Usage

measure(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'character'
measure(x, backend, instrument, ...)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
measure(
  x,
  backend,
  instrument,
  ...,
  text = NULL,
  id = NULL,
  image = NULL,
  keep = character(0),
  num_ctx = "auto",
  items = NULL,
  checkpoint = NULL,
  verbosity = c("normal", "quiet", "verbose")
)

Arguments

x

A character vector of documents, or a data frame.

...

Passed to methods by the generic. On a method it is not used, and is refused if anything reaches it, since every argument after it is name-only and a misspelling would otherwise be swallowed.

backend

An ollama_backend() object.

instrument

An instrument().

text

A string naming the column holding document text. Optional when image names one, so a picture with no caption is a corpus. Default is NULL.

id

A string naming an identifier column. Defaults to the integer row index.

image

A string naming a column holding media sent alongside the prompt rather than inside it. A character column is one picture per document. A list column is several, one element per document holding its paths in order, which is how a video window arrives. Nothing is shared between calls, so a run costs documents times items at close to full price, and a window of K frames costs K encodes on every call. prepare_image() builds a corpus in the character shape. Default is NULL.

keep

A character vector of additional columns to carry into the results. Names must be unique, and a column whose name the results already use is refused, since both copies would come back suffixed and the name would then read as NULL. Rename it in x first.

num_ctx

An integer giving the context window ceiling, or "auto". Left unset, Ollama allocates the model's full window and the cache that goes with it whether the prompts need it or not, which on a local machine is memory taken from elsewhere. Setting the ceiling to what the corpus needs returns it. Setting it too low truncates silently, since llama.cpp keeps the tail and the answer looks ordinary, and the size needed is not knowable by inspection because documents and questions both vary and the answer needs room after both.

So "auto" (the default) measures it. The longest document by word count is sent once with no ceiling and its token count read back, then rounded up with headroom. An integer is used as given, for a corpus already known. NULL or NA sends no ceiling and lets Ollama choose, in which case the truncated column is NA for every row. A resumed run uses whatever its checkpoints were written under, overriding all of these.

items

A character vector of item names to restrict the run to, or NULL (the default) for every item.

checkpoint

A string giving the directory for per-document .rds files, or NULL (the default) to hold everything in memory.

verbosity

A string setting how much to report. Each level is the one before it plus more.

  • "quiet" reports progress and the run summary only.

  • "normal" is the default. It adds the header, meaning a title over one line each for the model, the context ceiling, the first token the backend check read, and the size of the job.

  • "verbose" adds one line per item, with its winning label, probability, leaked mass, and wall time.

Every check runs at every level. Only the reporting changes. "quiet" is for loops over several instruments against one corpus, where the caller states the configuration once rather than once per call. For no output at all, wrap the call in suppressMessages(). Progress is a bar redrawn in place in an interactive session, and a line every ten documents anywhere else, such as a knitted document or a log.

Value

A fathom_results object. A list of two frames, with the run's provenance on its attributes. $probs holds one row per document, item and label. $calls holds one row per document and item, carrying everything that describes the answer rather than any one label, so it is stored once instead of repeating down the label rows.

Keys, in both frames, and what a join is on

  • id is the document identifier, from the id column or from the names of a character vector.

  • item names which instrument question produced the row.

$probs, differing down the labels of one call

  • label is the label this row scores, in the order the instrument declares them.

  • prob_renorm is the probability of this label rescaled so the labels sum to 1. The measure. NA when no label appeared at all, since there is nothing to condition on, and exactly 0 for a label that fell outside the top_logprobs alternatives. The raw probability, against every token the model could have written, is prob_renorm * (1 - prob_other).

$calls, one row per document and item

Anything named in keep rides here too, since a carried column describes the document rather than any one label.

  • error is the message when the call failed, otherwise NA, so a call succeeded exactly when error is NA.

  • truncated is TRUE when the prompt came within 64 tokens of num_ctx, so the document may have lost its opening.

  • top1_token is the token the model actually generated, whether or not it counts as a label.

  • prob_other is the mass on tokens counting as no label. The diagnostic that says whether the question landed. It is exactly 1 when no label appeared anywhere in the returned distribution.

  • margin is the gap between the top two prob_renorm values. What inspect_cases() sorts on to find the closest calls above two labels.

  • expected_score is prob_renorm weighted by the instrument's scores. NA for an instrument built without them.

  • prompt_hash is the hash of the assembled prompt. What checkpoint invalidation matches on, and not for reading.

On the attributes, constant for the run

instrument and backend as given, model, num_ctx as resolved, exclusive, and run_at.

Prompt ordering

The document goes before the question, and items for a document run contiguously, so Ollama's prefix cache prefills the document once per document rather than once per item.

Checkpointing

Checkpointing is off by default. Supply checkpoint to enable it. One .rds per document holds the full record plus provenance, and a document whose items are all current is skipped without a model call. There is no separate resume function. Calling this twice against the same directory does only what is outstanding.

Invalidation is per item, keyed on a hash of the question, cue, labels, scaffolding, and model. Rewording one item re-extracts that item across the corpus at question-only cost, since the first call still warms the document cache. This is not proportionally cheap. A partial rerun still pays the full document prefill for every row.

scores are the exception, and they are outside the hash on purpose. Rescaling an ordinal instrument changes no token the model sees, so re-extracting would be waste. The expected score is instead recomputed from the stored probabilities against whatever instrument is in hand, on this path and in read_checkpoints(), so a rescaled resume returns the new arithmetic without spending a call.

There is no schema tag. A change to scoring code that leaves prompts unchanged will not invalidate anything. Delete the directory by hand.

Cost of num_ctx = "auto"

One extra call per measure() invocation, not per document. Running several instruments over the same corpus measures once each, because a different instrument means a different prompt and therefore a different token count. Passing an integer once the corpus is known skips it.

Retrying failures

A failed item is stored with its reason in error and is therefore stale on the next pass, so re-running retries exactly those. There is no separate retry sweep, which would run against a cold cache.

When the check before the first document fails

Before any document, measure() sends one prompt built from your instrument and the corpus document nearest the median word count, or a built-in question when the corpus has no text. Among other checks, the run starts only if the first generated token is one of your labels. When it is not, nothing is measured and the message names the token the model opened with.

Three causes are known. The cue may not name the labels clearly enough, which preview() shows. The chat template may open a reasoning block although reasoning is off on every call, which is a property of the model's template rather than of your instrument. Or the model may open with prose, a word such as The or Okay before its answer.

Worked examples in the question, each a short document followed by its one-word answer, are the known fix for prose. Without them Qwen3.8-27B answered 941 of 945 tweets in full sentences in Denney and DiGiuseppe's (2026) replication of a tweet-sentiment study, and with them its answers could be scored. Examples become part of the instrument, so validate and audit the instrument that carries them.

Character input

A character vector stores the documents on the results in a docs attribute, so the audit functions find them without a docs argument. Ids are the vector's names when it has them, and its positions otherwise.

A data frame does not, and measure() never writes the document into a column. It reads the one you name and keeps a hash of the assembled prompt. Carrying the text instead would put a copy of the corpus in $calls, once per item, and the results are the object that gets saved.

Naming that column in keep carries it deliberately, and then it is a kept column like any other rather than something the schema promises.

References

Denney, S. and DiGiuseppe, M. (2026). JEV versus LLMs. Accuracy, cost and calibration on seven political science replications. arXiv:2610.06625.

See also

ollama_backend() and instrument() for its two inputs, preview() for the prompt it sends, read_checkpoints() for a run cut short, and item_report() and inspect_cases() for reading what comes back.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Needs a running Ollama server, so it is not run here.
oll <- ollama_backend("gemma4:31b")
b <- instrument(
  items = "Where does this sentence fall on the six-point sentiment scale?",
  labels = c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"),
  exclusive = TRUE
)
res <- measure(parlasent, instrument = b, backend = oll, text = "sentence",
  id = "id")
res$probs
} # }
